subject: plotting locations from DISTANCE Sampling transect detections

messages.author: f2777afe52b659e4
messages.subject: plotting locations from DISTANCE Sampling transect detections
parts:
Dear Colleagues,

I am looking for an extension/tool in ArcView/GIS in order to plot
transect data (location of detections) collected
with DISTANCE Sampling.

So I have (i) location on the transect, (ii) forward distance and (iii)
forward angle (radial angles; instead of a purely perpendicular
distance. Although this could be obtained via an easy sin formula) of
the detected object. These data are in an Excel or similar table for
import in ESRI.

If one works in meters, e.g. flat UTM, one could probably figure this
out by oneself, but when dealing with Lat Lon and projections over
larger areas it might get trickier.

Eventually, I would like to plot these true locations of the
objects/animals detected along the transect onto a GIS habitat map etc.

Thanks for any advice; best regards

Falk

messages.author: 17b53ceda886e27f
messages.subject: Re: plotting locations from DISTANCE Sampling transect detections
parts:
Dear Falk, list,

I think there are a lot of free extensions and tools available at ESRI's
website. Search for "distance and azimuth" at http://arcscripts.esri.com/=

But as far as I know all tools require a projected coordinate system as
calculating new coordinates on a 3D surface of a geographic coordinate
system is quite complex. But I think errors should remain small if you us=
e a
suitable projection. Moreover I think as distance measurement units are
rather small (i.e. meters, rarely kilometers) in comparison to the extent=
of
your entire survey area, so errors due to projecting your coordinates wil=
l
be acceptable (in general distance measurement errors will be larger than=

projection errors). If you are using ArcView check the web site mentioned=

above, if you are already using ArcGIS I can send you some python
geoprocessing scipts developed for line transects, which read projected o=
r
unprojected observer positions (on the transect) from a dbase file, conve=
rt
the coordinates to a different projection (optional), and compute object
positions based on the projectd coordinates, distances, and (geographic)
angles stored in the attribute table.

Hope this helps and best regards

=09Felix
